string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing, the capital of the People\'s Republic of China, is the country\'s political, cultural, international-exchange and scientific-innovation centre. Located in the north of the North China Plain and partly surrounded by Hebei Province, it is one of four municipalities directly under the central government. With a permanent population of around 21.8 million, the city has more than 3,000 years of recorded history. It is home to world-famous landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Great Wall and the Temple of Heaven, and it hosted the 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games. Beijing remains a global centre of heritage and modern development.

Shanghai is a municipality directly under the central government of China and one of the world\'s leading global financial centres. Situated at the estuary of the Yangtze River in East China and facing the Pacific Ocean, it is part of the dynamic Yangtze River Delta. With a permanent population of about 24.8 million, Shanghai is one of China\'s largest cities. The city is known for its historic Bund waterfront, the modern Pudong skyline, and its status as China\'s biggest economic hub and busiest container port. It blends traditional culture with a vibrant, open international atmosphere.

Chongqing is a municipality directly under the central government in southwestern China and the largest of China\'s municipalities by population and land area, home to more than 32 million people. Often called the "Mountain City", it rises in dramatic tiers where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet, with about three-quarters of its territory mountainous or hilly. It serves as the economic centre of the upper Yangtze region and a major national manufacturing and transport hub. Chongqing is widely famous for its spicy hotpot and malatang cuisine, as well as its dramatic night-time skyline and rich wartime capital heritage.

Tianjin is a municipality directly under the central government located in northern China, about 120 kilometres from Beijing, and is the largest coastal city in North China. Situated on the Bohai Bay and the lower reaches of the Hai River, it has long been an important port and industrial centre. With a permanent population of around 13.6 million, Tianjin developed as a major treaty port in the nineteenth century and retains rich European-style architecture alongside modern districts such as the Binhai New Area. It is known for its cultural heritage, baozi dumplings and its key role in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei regional development.
